facts.text: My eyesight has been getting worse.
It's been going on for 2 weeks.
My eyes don't hurt; there's no pain with it.
A month ago I was prescribed reading glasses.
They haven't made my vision any better.
I don't have any medical problems.
I drink about 14 units of alcohol a week.
I admit my diet is poor.
For breakfast I have tea with milk and toast.
I often skip lunch, or just have a packet of crisps.
Dinner is usually meat and potatoes.
I only eat green leafy vegetables once or twice a month.

aliases: nutritional optic neuropathy due to folate deficiency
gold.reasoning: 1. Nutritional optic neuropathy considered because of poor dietary intake and classic central scotomas — “it is important that a careful history is taken when evaluating patients with suspected optic neuropathy … low intake of green leafy vegetables should be actively sought.” 2. Toxic optic neuropathy due to alcohol and tobacco less likely because moderate consumption and visual improvement occurs despite continued use in folate deficiency — “vision can return to normal with vitamin supplementation … despite no modification of alcohol/tobacco consumption.” 3. Leber’s hereditary optic neuropathy excluded by patient demographics and nutritional correlations — “LHON … is more common in young men” and is a mitochondrial disorder not directly linked to diet. 4. Demyelinating optic neuropathy ruled out by MRI findings showing no evidence of demyelination — “MRI … revealed … no evidence of demyelination.”

x002: The source does not date the field, disc and colour-vision tests (s004-s006); they follow the 9-day examination in the narrative and are given the same time.
x011: The source reports thyroid function tests as 'negative'; probably normal.

leakage.reason: 'optic discs' is anatomy in the fundoscopy result; the result is normal and does not name the neuropathy.

source_issues: Reading glasses were prescribed one month before presentation, but the visual deterioration is a 2-week history; the glasses may have been for an earlier, unrelated need.
Vitamin B12 354 nmol/l is implausibly high in nmol/l; probably pmol/l or ng/l.
notes: Index visit: the presentation with a 2-week history of progressive painless bilateral visual deterioration (s001); the eye examination 9 days later and the laboratory tests and MRI of the same workup are findings with time where given.
The visual acuity of 6/60 records a decline after presentation; it is kept as a timed finding and not as a new patient fact.
Gold-term warnings for 'serum folate' and 'red cell folate' are kept: these are the tests' clinical names.
The diet is a present 'poor diet' habit fact with the meal pattern and green-vegetable frequency as children.
